app.name: B.O.P.E Scanner
app.tagline: Offline PC check for Roblox screenshares. Shows evidence and where it came from — never says a PC is clean.

start.title: What do you want to do?
start.self_hint: See everything, only on this screen.
start.ss_hint: For staff watching your screen. Asks for your consent first and shows what matches a rule, with a timeline of the times the consent lists.
start.elevate_hint: Some checks need administrator rights. This closes the program, starts it again with those rights and scans from the beginning. Windows will ask you to confirm.
start.elevate_declined: You declined the Windows prompt. Nothing changed.
start.elevate_failed: Windows did not start the program with administrator rights. Nothing changed.
start.scan_note: The scan ran on this PC when the program started, before this window opened, so the window cannot change the results. Nothing is shown or saved until you choose.
start.full_done: This was a full scan: you agreed in the Windows dialog before it read anything.
start.full_hint: Reads more than the standard scan: the name of each server cache folder FiveM for GTA V Enhanced keeps, and the kinds of words in PowerShell's commands, never the commands. This closes the program and starts it again; before it reads anything, a Windows dialog lists what a full scan reads and asks you. No there gives you the standard scan.
start.full_failed: Windows did not start the program again. Nothing changed.

consent.title: Before you share your screen
consent.reads: When it started, this program read, on this PC: security settings such as Secure Boot — as Windows and as the firmware report it — memory integrity, and the PowerShell logging policies of this PC and of the Windows account running this program, and whether the speculative-execution mitigations, SEHOP and the kernel object-namespace protection are switched off, and whether the firmware describes an IOMMU; the programs running and when each started, and the files in FiveM's plugin folders for GTA V Legacy and Enhanced and FiveM.exe itself, with their signatures (Authenticode); for FiveM's log, crash and cache folders for GTA V Legacy and Enhanced: how many files and subfolders each holds, their total size and the earliest and latest file times, and for each Enhanced server cache folder when it was created and last changed and how many entries it holds, and for Legacy's resource cache, its index folder's own times, how many files it holds and the latest of their times, never a file or folder name; these times can match two reports of this PC; what Windows recorded about programs that ran (Prefetch, BAM, Program Compatibility Assistant), and whether Prefetch is switched on, and for a running program or one of these records whose file is below FiveM's program folder, which edition's it was (Legacy or Enhanced), never the path; how many events of each kind the Windows event logs hold, not what the events say, and which file and size Windows sets for each log; whether a Prefetch or event log file is marked read-only; how many records the change journal of the Windows drive holds and when the oldest and newest were written, and for the Prefetch, event log and Program Compatibility Assistant folders, FiveM's plugin folders and the folder PowerShell keeps its command history in, how many records name each folder and how many of those created, deleted, renamed or changed a file, never a file name; the drivers registered with Windows: each driver service's name and start setting, where its file is, and that file's SHA-256; what Windows starts by itself: each program service's name and start setting, each Run and RunOnce value's name, and each scheduled task's name, whether it is on and what starts it, with the file each one starts — where it is and, outside the Windows folder, its SHA-256 and signature (Authenticode); never the arguments a program is given; Microsoft Defender's exclusions: each folder, program and file type Defender is told not to scan, and how many network addresses it is told to skip, never the addresses; the settings that decide where network traffic goes, never a record of where it went: the lines of the hosts file that give a name under cfx.re, fivem.net or rockstargames.com an address, with that address (other lines are only counted), whether a proxy is on and whether a proxy server or a setup script is set, never their addresses, and the Windows Firewall rules for programs in FiveM's folders, with how many rules there are; what Windows says this installation is — the edition, the build, the registered organisation and the manufacturer, model and support link Settings shows, never the registered owner's name — and how each of the services Windows ships with (Defender, Windows Update, Error Reporting, Event Log, SysMain, Diagnostic Policy, Search, telemetry) is set to start, or that its key is not there; whether six named places are on this PC: five that the Atlas and ReviOS Windows modifications install, and the folder Windows keeps Defender's engine in — whether each is there and nothing about what is inside it; when parts of this PC were set up, as dates and never times: when this Windows installation was installed or last feature-upgraded, the earliest installation date Windows Setup kept and how many it kept, when the Windows drive's change journal, its root folder and its $Recycle.Bin were created, and when FiveM's program folders were created; these dates can match two reports of this PC; the PCI devices Windows remembers, present or not: the maker, device and subsystem numbers and the class Windows records, the driver bound to each, its problem code, and when Windows set it up, last saw it at a start of Windows and recorded it removed, never a serial number; how Windows started each time its System log remembers: one number per start that says whether it followed a full shutdown or a Fast Startup one, and nothing else of that event; these times can match two reports of this PC; and when Windows last started, which staff will see as one time at the top of the report.
consent.shows: Staff will see what matches a rule, and a timeline of: the times Windows recorded (Prefetch, BAM, Program Compatibility Assistant) for programs named FiveM.exe, GTA5.exe, GTA5_Enhanced.exe, PlayGTAV.exe or FiveM_b<number>_GTAProcess.exe, a name that does not show which program it was; the times of FiveM's log, crash and cache folders; the oldest and newest record of each event log; the first and last time the Code Integrity log recorded Windows refusing to load a file and Microsoft Defender's log recorded a detection, never which file or what was detected; the first and last time Windows PowerShell's log recorded a script block PowerShell itself flagged as suspicious, never what the script said; and the oldest and newest change the change journal holds for each folder it counts. It also shows how far back each of these records reaches — for each event log, Prefetch, BAM, Program Compatibility Assistant, the change journal and FiveM's folders, how many entries it holds and the oldest time still there, never a name — beside the dates above, and, when Prefetch or BAM reaches back further than FiveM's folders were last written and holds none of the names above, one statement that puts the two side by side with the ordinary reasons for it; and, for each FiveM edition, one statement that puts its last session — when it began and ended, from a FiveM process running now, Prefetch or BAM, never compared with the scan's time — beside how long before or after its start its own folders were written, with the ordinary reasons for that. Your user name is hidden in file paths. A hosts line's address is shown only as its kind: loopback, unspecified, private or public. The name of a Run value or a scheduled task is not shown.
consent.sends: aeterna-rongroi's own code sends nothing anywhere.
consent.webview: This window uses Microsoft WebView2, a Windows component that may send Windows diagnostic data according to your Windows settings. The CLI version does not use WebView2.
consent.agree: I agree — show the SS view
consent.full_reads: A full scan also read the name of each server cache folder FiveM for GTA V Enhanced keeps — one per server this PC joined — with when it was created and last changed. What the name is made from is not known; it stays the same for that server on this PC, so it can match two reports of this PC. It also read the words in PowerShell's commands, kept only as kinds — whether a command downloaded something and ran it, told Microsoft Defender to look away, cleared a log or history, or named FiveM — from the history of commands typed into a PowerShell window, the scripts Windows PowerShell flagged as suspicious, and the command lines it was started with. No command was kept; the one thing kept is the name of a website a command downloaded from.
consent.server_identity: Also show which servers these are (the folder names). Off: each name is shown as %SERVER_IDENTITY%.
consent.download_host: Also show the name of each website a PowerShell command downloaded from. Off: each name is shown as %DOWNLOAD_HOST%.

declined.title: Nothing was shown
declined.body: You refused. No results were shown or saved. You can close this window.

home.title: Roblox PC check
home.purpose: Reads traces Windows keeps about programs, files, devices and settings, explains each finding with its ordinary explanations, and shows everything on this screen while you share it.
home.rights_user: standard user — some sources will not be read
home.info_failed: The program's details could not be read.
home.elevate_hint: Several sources (Prefetch, event logs, drivers, AppCompatCache, firmware) need administrator rights. Restarting asks Windows to confirm and opens this screen again; nothing is read before you start.
home.elevate_declined: You declined the Windows prompt. Nothing changed.
home.elevate_failed: Windows did not start the program with administrator rights.
home.mode_ss_hint: For a checker watching your screen: shows what matches a rule and the timeline; hides your user name in paths and everything that matched nothing.
home.mode_self_hint: Shows everything that was read, including what matched no rule.
home.tier_standard_hint: Execution traces, Roblox, processes, persistence, drivers, devices, network settings and logs. About one to two minutes.
home.tier_full_hint: Everything in the standard scan, plus the sources below, which hold more personal information:

reads.roblox_tools: names matching a catalog of Roblox launchers, FastFlag tools, FPS unlockers, executors and injectors — only matching names — in AppData, Temp, ProgramData, Program Files, Downloads, Desktop, Documents, inside .zip, .rar and .7z archives (nothing extracted) and in your Recycle Bin; correlated with every other source
reads.roblox: the Roblox player and files beside it, client settings count, logs' times, bootstrappers; executor-style folders and which executor-only functions their scripts call
reads.fastflags: Roblox FastFlag files (ClientAppSettings.json in Roblox and launcher folders, FastFlag tools' settings): counts by kind and names of network/physics flags, never values
reads.processes_memory: running programs, the Roblox player's loaded modules and executable memory counts (when its anti-cheat allows), programs running from user folders
reads.execution: Prefetch, BAM, PCA, UserAssist, MuiCache, FeatureUsage and AppCompatCache records of programs; shortcuts (.lnk) to Roblox tools or programs in your folders; Amcache and the SRUM database (CPU use per program) from an existing shadow copy (none is created); in the advanced scan, ShellBags and the Open/Save dialog list, only paths with catalog names
reads.files: change-journal counts for watched folders; in the advanced scan, programs and scripts in Downloads, Desktop and Documents; catalog names in the change journal and inside .zip, .rar and .7z archives (index only, nothing extracted); in the advanced scan, catalog names in the NTFS Master File Table, including records of deleted files (metadata only); this account's Recycle Bin: for each item its $I (original path, size, deletion time) and the times of its $I and $R entries, never the deleted file itself
reads.persistence: services, Run keys, scheduled tasks, Defender exclusions, IFEO debuggers, AppInit_DLLs, Winlogon, permanent WMI subscriptions (never a script's text)
reads.drivers: registered drivers with their SHA-256 and known-vulnerable driver lists
reads.macros_peripherals: macro tools and scripts by name, devices that act as keyboards or mice
reads.usb_devices: USB, HID and PCI devices Windows remembers (never serial numbers), setupapi installs
reads.browser_scripts: PowerShell logging and, in the advanced scan, browser extensions' permissions (never history, cookies or passwords)
reads.network: hosts file names, proxy settings, firewall rules for game folders, network adapters (never addresses or traffic)
reads.system_logs: how many events of each kind the event logs hold and when, log clearing records; the state of five Windows services (PcaSvc, DiagTrack, DPS, SysMain, EventLog) from the Service Control Manager, query rights only, and their state and start-type events in the System log
reads.firmware_boot: Secure Boot, memory integrity, TPM, test signing, IOMMU, BIOS identity, virtual-machine hints
reads.other: what Windows says it is, Windows modifications, installed programs

home.promise_offline: Works offline: this program's own code sends nothing anywhere.
home.promise_readonly: Changes nothing it examines: no file, key, service, driver or setting is written or removed.
home.promise_private: Never reads passwords, cookies, tokens, messages, documents' contents or payment data.
home.promise_visible: Every step is shown here; you can cancel at any time and close the program.
home.promise_ss: SS mode hides your user name in paths and lists only what matches a rule.
home.limits: No software check can prove a PC is clean: it cannot see another PC, DMA hardware, compromised firmware or a freshly reinstalled Windows.
home.show_download_host: Also show the website names files and commands were downloaded from (off: shown as %DOWNLOAD_HOST%)
home.agree: I have read what will be examined and I agree
home.refuse_ok: You may refuse: close the program and nothing is read.

scan.title: Checking this PC
scan.live_none: Nothing has matched a rule yet.
scan.live_note: Preliminary: the final report separates this program's own traces and adds the assessment.
scan.cancelled_body: The check stopped before it finished. No report was built or saved.

ui.brand_line: Offline PC check · evidence, never a verdict

state.report_failed: The report could not be read.

overview.tools_note: Correlated across every source; see Evidence
overview.services_note: Current state and System log history
overview.recycle_note: Times of this account's Recycle Bin
overview.timeline_note: Every time the view may show, in order

time.unrecognised: Not a time this program reads; shown exactly as received

timeline.zone_note: Times are shown in {{zone}}; hover a time for UTC and the value as received.

services.intro: A stopped or disabled service is not, on its own, a sign of cheating: tuning guides, editions, policies and updates stop these services. It only says why another source may hold less.
services.not_read: The services could not be read.
services.source_scm: Source: Service Control Manager, query rights only
services.partial: Some services could not be queried: {{reason}}
services.history_intro: Events 7034, 7036, 7040 and 7045 of the Service Control Manager for these services, newest first. The log keeps what its size allows; an older change may no longer be in it.
services.history_not_read: The history could not be read: {{reason}}
services.history_none: The System log holds no event of these services.

role.pca: Program Compatibility Assistant; feeds the PCA records of programs that ran.
role.dps: Diagnostic Policy Service; feeds diagnostics, including SRUM data.
role.eventlog: Windows Event Log; writes the event logs every log source reads.

recycle.intro: This account's Recycle Bin on the system drive, read without opening any deleted file. Nothing is restored, moved or removed. An item missing from the bin is never read as a deliberate deletion.
recycle.not_read: The Recycle Bin could not be read.
recycle.last_change: Last modification observed in the artifact

last_change_source.folder: Observed on the bin folder's own write time
last_change_source.entry: Observed on one of its $I/$R entries

recycle.last_change_note: There is no single "modified at" for the Recycle Bin. This is the newest write time found on the folder or its entries. Emptying the bin also writes the folder, so a folder time newer than every entry is consistent with an emptying — and with anything else that wrote the folder.
recycle.newest_deletion_note: Written by Windows inside the $I file when the item was moved to the bin
recycle.orphans_note: A $I without its $R: the content was removed by other means. A $R without its $I: its index is gone. Neither says who did it or why.
recycle.capped: More $I files than this program reads in one check; the rest were counted, not read.
recycle.ss_note: SS mode shows only items whose name matches the Roblox tool catalog.
recycle.content_note: The $R's last-write time is usually kept from the file when it was moved to the bin on the same drive, but any program can set it: it is the artifact's time, not the file's history.

reports.html: For reading in a browser; offline, no script, no request to any host.
reports.txt: Plain text, for pasting in a ticket.
reports.json: The view as data, with ISO 8601 times exactly as recorded.
reports.pdf: For printing or attaching; carries the SHA-256 of the equivalent JSON.
reports.times: Every file writes each time in UTC (ISO 8601 in JSON) and, in HTML, TXT and PDF, also in this computer's zone ({{zone}}), with the same kinds of time this window shows.

settings.title: Display
settings.time_note: Changes only how this window shows times. Every time is kept as recorded, in UTC, and the other reading stays one line below.
